title: Honest Sequential DCB Intervals under Unknown Shrinking Stagewise Overlap Scales
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded subfield below the mandatory field floor (paper score ceiling 7.1 < 7.4; salvageable=false); typed math review also found unrepaired identification-missing-history defects in two causal coverage theorems.
gap_reasons: The matched minimax expected-length result is proved only on the declared two-branch class, whose information-branch assumption excludes intermediate high-dimensional rare-path regimes.
necessity of the high-dimensional correction remains open, so the ambient result is a bracket rather than a general frontier.

The derivation of (12) conditions the second-stage regression on H_1, but ass:second-stage-ignorability and the definition of m_2 condition only on H_2; without H_1 being measurable from H_2 (or Y(1,1) mean-independent of H_1 given H_2,A_1,X), E[Y(1,1)|H_1,A_1,X]=E[m_2(H_2)|H_1,A_1,X] does not follow, so the interval need not cover psi.

Its equation (1) repeats the invalid tower step: H_2 was not specified to contain H_1, while second-stage ignorability is only conditional on H_2; hence the claimed observed-law identification and the ambient coverage/length conclusions are not established on the declared class.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 constructed a count-capped sequential DCB interval, a restricted-class length argument, a product-only-overlap obstruction, and an ambient-class upper bracket. D0.5 graded the package subfield below the mandatory field floor and found an undeclared H_1/H_2 history relation in two identification proofs. Those coverage claims remain unproved as banked; a nested-history repair and a matching ambient high-dimensional converse remain open.
tldr: For separately comparable but unknown stage scales, the calibrated count-capped sequential DCB interval remains finite-sample honest and rate-optimal on the declared two-branch class. On the larger ambient class, a second explicit three-way-split interval is total, scale-blind, and finite-sample honest, with expected-length upper correction \(\rho(N,p,s)=\min\{1,s t_p/N,\sqrt{t_p/N}\}\) and a root-information all-procedure lower bound. The bracket matches when \(s t_p=O(\sqrt m)\), while a matching converse for the high-dimensional \(\rho\) terms remains open. The independent-block Gaussian refinement still applies under \(s\log(n(p\vee2))/\sqrt{nrab}\to0\).
gap: Published DCB inference fixes a positive stagewise overlap constant, while published decaying-overlap theory treats one selection gate. Neither makes recursive caps and fallback decisions observable under two unknown shrinking scales, nor supplies finite-sample honesty and a matched expected-length frontier.
fill: The project constructs one scale-blind interval, calibrates its all-procedure rate with explicit same-class two-point laws, derives an explicit block-studentized Gaussian regime, and proves both a fully specified compound-Poisson finite-event boundary and a product-only-overlap obstruction for the published sequential minimum-norm program and its feasible scalar-cap relaxations.
